**Live: 29.1× real time, 6.85% WER · Final (commit pass at utterance ends): 14.2×, 5.06% WER**

![ULTRA: Reproducible Streaming Speech Recognition on One CPU Core. Single-core throughput against pooled WER on the 730-utterance LibriSpeech DEV panel](docs/paper/money.png)

**Figure 1.** One INT8 model on one quiet Zen 2 core: ULTRA v3.0.0 (live) runs at 29.1× (0.344 W, 6.85% WER); the final mode reaches 5.06% at 14.2× (0.720 W) vs. 14.5×, 5.25% for Zipformer INT8. WER is common across all 730 utterances of the LibriSpeech DEV panel (400 dev-clean + 330 dev-other, unified `ultra-score` normaliser). Throughput is the median of three cold runs on one pinned Zen 2 core, model load included (4 interim rows use shared host H0 (‡); 3 slow rows time the 73-clip subset (§)). The speed axis is linear. Blue diamonds link the live and utterance-segmented final modes of our single `v3.0.0` INT8 artifact. Filled circles stream live; hollow circles decode offline whole clips; lighter circles are interim shared-host (H0) rows. Active core W per stream (core energy registers, same run), not device power. DEV-only measurements. [Read the paper](docs/paper/paper.pdf) · [v3.0.0 release record](docs/ultra/releases/v3.0.0.md).

ULTRA is a small streaming Conformer transducer and an integer-exact pure-Rust CPU engine. One prepared INT8 artifact (`v3.0.0`) provides two operating points on the exact same weights—both on the quiet full-panel H1 speed–WER Pareto frontier: in the quiet full-panel H1 cohort, **live** greedy 160 ms streaming is the fastest system on one CPU core (29.1× vs. 14.5× for Zipformer INT8, 2.0×), with the lowest active core W/stream (0.344 W vs. 0.591 W) and smallest footprint (74 MB vs. 153 MB) at 6.85% pooled panel WER; the utterance-segmented **final** commit pass (0.720 W, 725 MB) runs within 2% of Zipformer's single-core speed (14.2× utterance-segmented vs. 14.5× streaming) while lowering pooled WER (5.06% vs. 5.25%). Trained on LibriSpeech 960 h plus Libri-Light pseudo-labelled by R0 (the Zipformer comparator); all results are LibriSpeech DEV only.

See the [benchmark freeze protocol](docs/ultra/FREEZE.md).

- **Accuracy.** On the 730-utterance LibriSpeech DEV panel, ULTRA v3.0.0 (final, seg.) (utterance-segmented commit pass) scores 5.06% pooled WER (3.25% dev-clean / 7.65% dev-other), ranking 6th of 15 complete-panel systems (beating 8 of 13 public comparators (including streaming Zipformer INT8 at 5.25%)); ULTRA v3.0.0 (live) on the exact same INT8 weights scores 6.85% pooled. On full LibriSpeech DEV (5,567 utt), final text reaches 5.48% pooled (2.92% clean / 8.20% other; live 7.45%). Larger models score lower at higher CPU cost on their respective timing hosts (3.56% for Nemotron 560 ms (shared-host timing) and 3.36% for Parakeet TDT v3 (onnx-asr, offline)).
- **Speed & memory.** ULTRA v3.0.0 (live) is the fastest system in the quiet full-panel H1 cohort at 29.1× real time (2.0× streaming Zipformer INT8) (3.4% of one quiet Zen 2 core, 74 MB peak RAM—smallest footprint vs. 153 MB for Zipformer INT8), against 14.5× for Zipformer INT8, 8.20× for Moonshine Tiny, 6.88× for Vosk Small, 6.69× for Parakeet TDT v3 (onnx-asr, offline), 5.92× for Parakeet TDT v3 (sherpa-onnx, offline), 4.13× for Vosk Large, 0.91× for Whisper.cpp Tiny and 0.42× for Whisper.cpp Base. ULTRA v3.0.0 (final, seg.) runs at 14.2× real time and 725 MB peak RAM (median final-text delay 211 ms after endpoint), within 2% of streaming Zipformer INT8's single-core speed (14.2× utterance-segmented vs. 14.5× streaming).
- **Watts.** Unpaced active core W per stream on quiet H1: 0.344 W for ULTRA v3.0.0 (live) (58% of Zipformer INT8's active core energy) and 0.720 W (1.64 W package) for ULTRA v3.0.0 (final, seg.), against 0.591 W for Zipformer INT8, 1.077 W for Moonshine Tiny and 1.711 W for Parakeet TDT v3 (sherpa-onnx, offline) (CPU domain only, not wall power).
- **Integer-exact INT8.** Per-row centred INT8 with exact int32 accumulation and portable log-mel matches FP32 PyTorch on full DEV (5,567 utterances) within −0.003 pp (95% bounds −0.033 to +0.028 pp), with repeatable, batch-invariant execution.

**Also measured, not ranked (subset WER, other hardware):** Parakeet unified (whole clip): 2.21% on `panel73` (M3 Ultra); Nemotron labs unified (whole clip): 2.33% on `panel73` (Xeon 8358); Nemotron labs unified (stream 160 ms): 7.74% on `panel10` (Xeon 8358).

**Always-on paced live capacity (quiet H1, one Zen 2 core, 128 s continuous stream of 22 DEV clips, `14s`):** 16 live `v3.0.0` streams paced at 1× fill 53.2% of one core at 0.358 W/stream net (0.364 W gross) core power and stable-word lag p50/p95 242/457 ms (1 stream: 6.2% busy, 0.487 W net, lag 190/420 ms; continuous-stream lag method, not directly ranked against per-clip `lag100` rows).
